description: Table 1 is a single-panel table rendered as an image, with no plots, micrographs or spectra; it lists the chemical compositions of three investigated steels. The header row reads "Steel", "Al", "Mn", "C", "Fe", separated by a single horizontal rule from three data rows. Row 1, steel "0.5C": Al 9.90, Mn 17.71, C 0.48, Fe "Bal.". Row 2, steel "0.8C": Al 9.91, Mn 17.14, C 0.77, Fe "Bal.". Row 3, steel "1.2C": Al 10.19, Mn 17.45, C 1.16, Fe "Bal.". Carbon is therefore the only deliberately varied element, rising from 0.48 to 0.77 to 1.16, while Al (9.90-10.19) and Mn (17.14-17.71) stay nearly constant and Fe is reported as balance. The table defines the alloy series used throughout the paper, Fe-18Mn-10Al-xC with x = 0.5, 0.8 and 1.2 C (wt%). The caption states the values are in mass %; the printed figure itself carries no unit symbols, no error bars and no footnotes other than "Bal." (balance).

observations.observation: The table header columns are, in order, 'Steel', 'Al', 'Mn', 'C', 'Fe', separated from the data by a single horizontal rule.
Steel '0.5C' is listed with Al 9.90, Mn 17.71, C 0.48 and Fe 'Bal.'.
Steel '0.8C' is listed with Al 9.91, Mn 17.14, C 0.77 and Fe 'Bal.'.
Steel '1.2C' is listed with Al 10.19, Mn 17.45, C 1.16 and Fe 'Bal.'.
Carbon is the only element varied systematically across the three rows (0.48, 0.77, 1.16), whereas Al (9.90-10.19) and Mn (17.14-17.71) are nearly constant.
The caption states that the tabulated values are chemical compositions in mass, %.
The citing text identifies the three steels as Fe-18Mn-10Al-xC (0.5, 0.8 and 1.2C, wt%) alloys.
The citing text reports calculated densities of 6.92, 6.88 and 6.78 g/cm3 for the 0.5C, 0.8C and 1.2C steels, respectively (not shown in the table).
The citing text reports austenite stacking fault energy values of 73.4 and 77.9 mJ/m2 for the 0.5C and 0.8C steels and 84.5 mJ/m2 for the 1.2C steel (not shown in the table).

The citing text describes processing of these steels: 50 kg ingots induction melted under argon, forged at 1200 C, hot rolled after 3 h homogenization at the same temperature to 3.5 mm (90% reduction), annealed at 1000 C for 1 h, cold rolled to 1 mm, then annealed at 1000 C and water quenched.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel with header row 'Steel, Al, Mn, C, Fe' and three data rows for steels 0.5C (9.90 Al, 17.71 Mn, 0.48 C, Bal. Fe), 0.8C (9.91 Al, 17.14 Mn, 0.77 C, Bal. Fe) and 1.2C (10.19 Al, 17.45 Mn, 1.16 C, Bal. Fe).
